In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new approach to NMR chemical shift calculation in proteins.
the development, application and validation of quantum-chemical methods for the prediction of NMR chemical shifts and other molecular properties.
the application of quantum-chemical methods to the computation of the 13 C α chemical shifts in proteins and the use of the computed values for structure refinement.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, at present, NMR chemical shifts can be computed to an acceptable degree of accuracy (r.m.s.d.=2–3 ppm) in proteins, but that this accuracy is not sufficient to provide a reliable means of structure refinement.

, at the present time, NMR chemical shifts can be used for structure refinement of proteins, but only if the protein structure is known with high accuracy (i.e. the bond lengths and bond angles are known with a precision of better than 0.02 Å and 1° respectively).

, for the proteins studied here, the quantum-chemical approach can provide a very good estimate of the experimental 13Cα shieldings, but the accuracy is limited by the quality of the input structure and the presence of conformational disorder.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, for the 13C chemical shifts of the protein backbone and side chains, the ‘optimized’ structures give results which compare favorably with experiment.
NMR chemical shift information can be incorporated into structure refinement procedures, and that this information will improve the quality of the refined structures.
the 13C chemical shifts of proteins are sensitive to the protein structure and that the quantum-chemical calculations can provide accurate values for comparison with experimental values.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the 13C chemical shift can be used to assess the quality of the protein structure, and that it may be used in conjunction with NMR chemical shift perturbations to detect structural changes upon binding.
, in proteins, 13Cα shielding calculations are a reliable tool for structure determination.
, in the context of protein NMR, the quantum-chemical computation of 13Cα shieldings can provide an independent and accurate means to validate the structure of a protein.
